items.descriptionAdvanced: Maseru is situated at an elevation of 1550 meters along the Caledon River, which forms the natural border with South Africa. As the seat of government and economic center of Lesotho, the city hosts major institutions and the Moshoeshoe I. International Airport. The city's development reflects the country's history since gaining independence in 1966. (Geography K7 — cities and regions)

Teyateyaneng is located northeast of Maseru in the Berea District and is a major center for traditional crafts, especially weaving. The name means 'place where it drifts' in the local Sesotho language, referring to the scenic surroundings. The city is an important stop for travelers wishing to explore the culture and crafts of the mountain kingdom. (Sachkunde K5 — crafts and culture)
